comments.author: @xalekcey
comments.text: For comparison. I live in Russia. My monthly salary is about $2,000. 5 years ago, I paid off the mortgage for a 3-room apartment (which I had been paying off for 11 years). The apartment is owned and I pay about $100 per month for utilities (there are no more payments for housing). For unlimited cellular Internet connection and unlimited home Internet (400 MB/s) about $ 20. About $400 per month for food (sometimes a restaurant and a take-home order). I also have a small country house of 120 sq.m. (you need to pay about $ 200 per year for it). Medical insurance is free, state-owned (good level of medicine). But there is always the opportunity to go to a private clinic (one appointment with a doctor costs about $ 40. An MRI scan is about 60-150 dollars at any moment, instantly). After all the necessary payments per month (rent, food, gasoline, communication), I have about 1300-1400 dollars left. There is a car, a motorcycle and an ATV for trips to hunting, fishing, and the forest.  Work 5 days a week, 8 hours a day. I have one job. I live a peaceful and happy life. The difference from the USA is in simple household details (I don't have a new Mercedes on credit or a big pickup truck, but a 2013 Toyota... I don't have a new iPhone, but a Chinese Android, and I don't have branded global brands, but local Russian or Chinese ones (which still fulfill their function). But Russia is not for everyone. These are traditional values, complex language, and a ruthless bureaucracy. I don't understand what's wrong in the USA. This has never happened before.
